subject.title: feat(agents): Swarm core — collector spawn, agents_wait, structured output, caps (gated)

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this broad persistent `tools.swarm` orchestration contract in core now, or require the Swarm program to be narrowed and staged before merge?
rationale: The PR adds a new gated user-facing configuration surface, gateway protocol fields, persistent registry state, and agent-runtime semantics; correctness fixes alone cannot determine the desired long-term core boundary.

options.title: Stage the core contract first
options.body: Keep this PR open, resolve the restart-safety defect and proof gap, and merge only after maintainers explicitly approve the configuration, persistence, and lifecycle boundary.

options.title: Narrow the first landing
options.body: Split the work so a smaller, explicitly approved collector/wait capability lands before scheduler, structured-output, and broader orchestration surfaces.

options.title: Keep Swarm outside core for now
options.body: Pause this branch and retain the program discussion until maintainers decide that persistent orchestration belongs in OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Stage the core contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open, resolve the restart-safety defect and proof gap, and merge only after maintainers explicitly approve the configuration, persistence, and lifecycle boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the linked Swarm program and the current implementation series, making them the best available routing candidate for the design decision.
